recipes.name: Bánh Mì Thịt
recipes.flavorProfile: A crackling, airy baguette layered with rich pâté, cool pork roll, five-spice roast pork belly, tangy pickles, cucumber, cilantro and a bite of chili.
recipes.healthBenefit: Brings protein from three kinds of pork and some iron and vitamin A from the liver pâté, with the pickles and fresh herbs adding crunch; it is a rich, salty sandwich best eaten as a full meal.

components.note: split along one side, warmed until crisp
about 30 g spread inside each roll
about 50 g sliced thin for each sandwich
about 1/4 tsp, for the pork rub

ingredients.baseName: Gris sidfläsk bit rå m. svål
ingredients.cutPrep: whole slab, flesh scored and skin pricked

ingredients.prepNote: 1 for the pork rub, 1 for the seasoning sauce

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)
Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Score the flesh side of the pork belly and prick the skin all over. Set it skin side up on a rack in the sink, pour boiling water over the skin and pat it dry.
Rub the flesh with the white pepper, five-spice and 1 clove of the garlic, rub the salt into the skin, and leave it uncovered in the fridge overnight.
Roast at 350°F (180°C) for 45 minutes, then put it under a hot grill for 15 to 20 minutes until the skin crackles. Rest it 15 minutes and slice thin.
Stir the soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar and the other garlic clove together for the seasoning sauce.
Warm the rolls at 350°F (180°C) for 3 to 5 minutes until the crust crackles, split each along one side, and spread pâté on one face and mayonnaise on the other.
Fill with chả lụa, roast pork, cucumber, pickled carrot and daikon, spring onion, cilantro and chili, spoon over a little seasoning sauce, and eat while the bread is still crisp.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the roast pork belly, chả lụa and pâté.
From the liver in the pâté.
A little from the cucumber, pickles, herbs and chili.

citations.source: Adam Liaw, Roast Pork Banh Mi
Helen's Recipes, Bánh Mì Thịt Nguội

recipes.curationNote: Pork rub, roasting and seasoning sauce from Adam Liaw (2 kg belly for 6 rolls), the rub scaled to a quarter for 500 g; the seasoning sauce, cucumber and spring onion kept at his amounts for 6 rolls. Layering from Helen's. Spring onion, cilantro and chili have no amounts in either source.

recipes.name: Bánh Mì Xíu Mại
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft pork and shrimp meatballs in a sweet, garlicky tomato sauce, spooned into a crisp roll so the bread soaks up the sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: The pork and shrimp bring protein and the tomato sauce adds lycopene and some vitamin C; the baguette makes it a filling, carb-heavy breakfast.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Mix the pork, shrimp, half the onion, jicama, salt, pepper, fish sauce, sugar, potato starch and scallion until tacky, and roll into balls about 3 cm across.
Steam the meatballs 10 to 12 minutes until firm, so they hold their shape in the sauce.
Heat the oil, fry the garlic and remaining onion 2 to 3 minutes, add the tomatoes and cook until they slump, 5 to 8 minutes.
Add the water, sugar, salt, fish sauce and 0.25 tsp pepper, slide in the meatballs and simmer 15 to 20 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Split the warm rolls, spoon in 3 or 4 meatballs with sauce, and top with pickles, cucumber and cilantro.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork and shrimp meatballs.
From the tomatoes cooked down in the sauce.

recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham, Vietnamese Meatballs (Xíu Mại) for every amount and step; serves 5, same as ours.

recipes.name: Bánh Mì Ốp La
recipes.flavorProfile: Runny fried eggs with lacy edges, seasoned with Maggi and black pepper, tucked into a crisp roll with chili sauce, cucumber, rau răm and chili.
recipes.healthBenefit: The eggs bring protein, choline and vitamin B12 for a quick breakfast; the roll supplies most of the energy.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
ingredients.prepNote: 1 tsp at 5.3 g per tsp; in place of Maggi seasoning sauce, which the database does not hold

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Slice the cucumber, rinse the rau răm and finely chop the chili.
Fry the eggs in the oil, keeping the yolks runny.
Split the rolls lengthwise, spread the chili sauce inside and lay in the cucumber.
Slide in the eggs, add the rau răm and chili and sprinkle with the salt, pepper and soy sauce. Close gently so the yolks do not break, and eat right away.

citations.source: Cookpad Vietnam, Bánh Mì Việt Nam Kẹp Trứng Ốp-la

recipes.curationNote: Cookpad Vietnam, Bánh Mì Việt Nam Kẹp Trứng Ốp-la for every amount and step; 1 sandwich, doubled to our 2: 1 baguette, 2 eggs fried with runny yolks, a little rau răm, chopped horn chili to taste, a few cucumber slices, chili sauce spread inside; oil, salt, pepper and soy sauce with no amounts.

recipes.name: Gỏi Cuốn (Fresh Spring Rolls)
recipes.flavorProfile: Cool, chewy rice paper wrapped around poached pork, pink shrimp, soft noodles, lettuce and mint, dipped into a thick sweet peanut hoisin sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lean protein from shrimp and pork with fresh lettuce and herbs, and nothing fried; the dip carries most of the sugar and salt.

components.note: about 1 tbsp per roll, for dipping

ingredients.baseName: Gris sidfläsk bit rå m. svål

ingredients.prepNote: 6 g in the pork water, 1.5 g in the shrimp water; most is poured away with the water
peeled and halved lengthwise after cooking

ingredients.baseName: Rice paper wrapper, soaked in water
ingredients.prepNote: 10 sheets, about 20 g each once dipped in water

instructions: Simmer the pork belly with the onion, sugar and 6 g salt in water to cover by 2 cm for 25 to 30 minutes, until cooked through; cool covered and slice paper thin.
Boil the shrimp in just enough water to cover with the remaining salt for 2 minutes, until pink, cool under cold water, then peel and halve each one lengthwise.
Boil the vermicelli 3 to 5 minutes, rinse in cold water and drain well.
Dip one sheet of rice paper in warm water for 2 to 3 seconds and lay it flat; it softens as you fill it.
Lay 3 shrimp halves cut side up in a row, then lettuce, noodles, mint and pork. Fold the sides in, roll tightly, and tuck a chive in so it pokes out of one end.
Serve right away with the peanut hoisin dip.

citations.source: Hungry Huy, How to Make Gỏi Cuốn

recipes.curationNote: Hungry Huy, How to Make Gỏi Cuốn for every amount and step; makes 10: 1/2 lb pork belly simmered with 1 onion, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp salt; 1/2 lb shrimp boiled with 1/4 tsp salt; lettuce, mint, chives, rice paper, rice noodles; peanut hoisin dip.

recipes.name: Chả Giò (Fried Spring Rolls)
recipes.flavorProfile: Shatteringly crisp golden rolls packed with juicy pork, glass noodles and crunchy wood ear, wrapped in lettuce and herbs and dunked in nước chấm.
recipes.healthBenefit: Brings protein from the pork, but deep frying makes these a rich treat; wrapping them in lettuce and herbs adds fresh greens to each bite.

components.note: about 1 tbsp per roll, for dipping

ingredients.baseName: Mushrooms, tree ears, Cloud ear, dried
Glass noodles made from mung bean starch
ingredients.cutPrep: soaked and cut in short lengths

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

ingredients.prepNote: 750 ml heated for deep frying; 75 ml counted as soaked up by the rolls, the rest stays in the pan

instructions: Mix the pork, wood ear, glass noodles, scallion, onion, sugar, pepper, sesame oil, salt and oyster sauce until evenly combined.
Lay a wrapper with a corner toward you, put a heaped tablespoon of filling near that corner and shape it into a log.
Fold the bottom corner over, fold in the sides, roll tightly and seal the last corner with egg yolk. Repeat with the rest.
Heat the oil to 325°F (165°C) and fry the rolls in small batches about 5 minutes, not touching, until golden brown.
Drain on a rack, then wrap each roll in lettuce with rau răm and perilla and dip it in nước chấm.

nutritionHighlights.note: Mostly from the pork and the frying oil.

citations.source: Vicky Pham, Vietnamese Egg Rolls (Chả Giò)

recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham, Vietnamese Egg Rolls (Chả Giò) for every amount and step; makes 30: 2 lb pork, 1/2 cup dried wood ear, 2 oz bean thread, 2 green onions, 1 small onion, 1 tsp sugar, 1/4 tsp pepper, 2 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp salt, 3 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tsp bouillon; served with lettuce and herbs such as sorrel, fish mint, rau răm and perilla.

recipes.name: Bánh Xèo (Crispy Pancakes)
recipes.flavorProfile: A sizzling, lacy yellow crêpe of rice flour, turmeric and coconut, folded over pork, shrimp and bean sprouts, then torn and rolled in mustard greens and herbs.
recipes.healthBenefit: Protein from pork and shrimp with a big pile of sprouts, greens and herbs; the coconut cream and frying oil make it a rich dish.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)
Gris sidfläsk bit rå m. svål

instructions: Whisk the rice flour, wheat flour, turmeric, water, coconut cream and salt into a thin batter, stir in the scallion and rest it 30 minutes.
Steam the soaked mung beans 15 to 20 minutes until soft.
Heat a 25 cm pan over high with a little oil, add a few slices of pork, 2 or 3 shrimp and some onion, and cook 1 to 2 minutes.
Pour in a ladle of batter and swirl it so it climbs the sides; it should sizzle loudly. Scatter a spoon of mung beans and a handful of sprouts over half.
Cover 2 to 3 minutes, then uncover and cook another 3 to 5 minutes until the edges are crisp and lift away. Fold in half and slide out.
Repeat with the rest. Eat torn into pieces, wrapped in mustard greens with herbs, and dipped in nước chấm.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork belly, shrimp and mung beans.
From the mustard greens and herbs.
From the coconut cream and pork belly.

recipes.curationNote: Hungry Huy amounts for 12 crêpes kept; fluid ounces converted to ml (28 fl oz water, 14 fl oz coconut cream). Southern style with coconut and mustard greens.

recipes.name: Bánh Khọt
recipes.flavorProfile: Bite-size cups of rice and coconut batter, crisp outside and custardy inside, each crowned with a shrimp and scallion oil, wrapped in lettuce and dipped.
recipes.healthBenefit: A shrimp on each cake brings a little protein and the lettuce and herbs add freshness; the coconut milk and pan oil make these a rich snack.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

ingredients.prepNote: for the cups of the pan

instructions: Whisk the rice flour, cornstarch, water, coconut milk, turmeric, salt and scallion into a smooth batter and rest it 30 minutes.
Heat a bánh khọt or aebleskiver pan over medium high and put about half a teaspoon of oil in each cup.
Fill each cup nearly to the top with batter; it should sizzle. Cover and cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Toss the shrimp with 0.25 tsp salt and a pinch of pepper.
Press a shrimp into each cake, cover again and cook 3 to 4 minutes more, until the bottoms are golden and crisp.
Lift out, spoon scallion oil over, and serve wrapped in lettuce and herbs with nước chấm.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the shrimp on each cake.
From the coconut milk in the batter.

recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham, Bánh Khọt for every amount and step; 14 cakes, same as ours; oil and herbs unmeasured in the source, ours keeps usual amounts.

recipes.name: Bánh Cuốn
recipes.flavorProfile: Silky, almost translucent steamed rice sheets rolled around savory pork and wood ear, topped with fried shallots and served with chả lụa and nước chấm.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light, steamed dish with protein from the pork and chả lụa; the fried shallots and dipping sauce add the salt.

components.note: about 1 tbsp scattered over each plate

ingredients.baseName: Mushrooms, tree ears, Cloud ear, dried

instructions: Whisk the rice flour, tapioca starch, salt, oil and water into a thin batter and rest it 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Heat the oil, cook the garlic and onion 2 minutes, add the pork and wood ear with salt, sugar and pepper and cook 5 to 7 minutes until dry and crumbly.
Brush a nonstick pan lightly with oil over medium heat, pour in a thin layer of batter, swirl, cover and steam 30 to 60 seconds until the sheet turns clear.
Turn the sheet onto an oiled tray, spoon a line of filling along one edge and roll it up. Repeat with the rest.
Plate the rolls with lettuce, sprouts, cucumber and sliced chả lụa, scatter fried shallots over, and pour nước chấm alongside.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork filling and chả lụa.
From the rice and tapioca sheets.

recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham's nonstick pan method and 5-serving amounts followed. Northern dish (Thanh Trì, Hà Nội), served as a plated breakfast, so side/main.

recipes.name: Phở Cuốn
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, wide sheets of fresh phở noodle rolled around garlicky stir-fried beef, lettuce and herbs, dipped in sweet sour nước chấm.
recipes.healthBenefit: The beef brings protein, iron and zinc, and the fresh herbs and lettuce add greens; nothing is fried in deep oil.

components.note: about 2 tbsp per serving, for dipping

instructions: Whisk the rice flour, tapioca starch, water, salt and oil and rest the batter 30 minutes.
Marinate the beef with garlic, ginger, fish sauce and pepper for 15 minutes.
Steam thin sheets of batter in a covered oiled pan for 1 to 2 minutes each, until clear, and stack them on an oiled tray. Cut each sheet into a rectangle about 15 by 20 cm.
Heat the oil over high, stir-fry the onion 1 minute, add the beef and cook 1 to 2 minutes, just until it loses its pink.
Lay lettuce, herbs and a spoon of beef on each sheet and roll it up tightly.
Serve with nước chấm for dipping.

citations.source: Helen's Recipes, Fresh Rice Noodle Rolls (Phở Cuốn)

recipes.curationNote: Helen's Recipes, Fresh Rice Noodle Rolls (Phở Cuốn) for every amount and step; serves 4: 1 cup rice flour, 1 cup tapioca starch, 2 cups water, 1/2 tsp salt, 2 tsp oil; 350 g beef, 1 tbsp garlic, 1 tsp ginger, 1/2 tsp pepper, fish sauce with no amount, 1 tbsp oil, 1 onion; lettuce, mint, perilla, cilantro; light fish sauce dip.

recipes.name: Bò Bía
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft rice paper rolls of sweet braised jicama and carrot, Chinese sausage, egg ribbons and dried shrimp, dipped in hoisin with crushed peanuts.
recipes.healthBenefit: The jicama and carrot bring fibre and vitamin A, and the eggs and dried shrimp add protein; the sausage and hoisin make it salty and sweet.

ingredients.baseName: Crustacean, processed shrimp, boiled and dried shrimp

ingredients.prepNote: cooked as a thin omelette and sliced
for cooking the jicama and carrot, cooked down

ingredients.baseName: Rice paper wrapper, soaked in water
ingredients.prepNote: 12 sheets, about 20 g each once dipped in water

instructions: Simmer the soaked dried shrimp, jicama and carrot with the salt in the cup of water, stirring, until tender but not mushy and most of the liquid has cooked off. Cool.
Pan-fry the sausage slices 2 to 3 minutes, and cook the eggs as a thin omelette and slice it into ribbons.
Warm the garlic in the 1/2 tsp oil, then stir in the hoisin, the 2 tbsp water and sugar and simmer 1 minute for the sauce.
Dip a sheet of rice paper, lay on lettuce, a spoon of jicama, sausage and egg, and roll tightly.
Serve with the hoisin sauce topped with crushed peanuts.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the eggs, sausage and dried shrimp.

recipes.curationNote: Hungry Huy, Bò Bía for every amount and step; serves 4: 3 to 4 tbsp dried shrimp, 1/2 lb jicama, 1 carrot, 2 tsp salt, 1 cup water, 3 sausages, 2 eggs; sauce 1 garlic clove, 1/2 tsp oil, 2 tbsp hoisin, 2 tbsp water, 1 tsp sugar, crushed peanuts.

recipes.name: Bánh Bột Lọc
recipes.flavorProfile: Clear, chewy tapioca dumplings showing an orange shrimp and pork filling, steamed in banana leaf and eaten with sweet fish sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: A small amount of protein from shrimp and pork in a mostly starchy dumpling; good as a snack rather than a meal.

ingredients.baseName: Gris sidfläsk bit rå m. svål
Crustacean, processed shrimp, boiled and dried shrimp

ingredients.name: banana leaves
ingredients.cutPrep: cut in 15 cm squares, wiped and softened over heat

instructions: Warm the oil with the annatto seeds 1 to 2 minutes until deep orange, then strain out the seeds.
Fry the shallot and garlic in the annatto oil, add the pork belly and dried shrimp and cook 5 to 7 minutes, seasoning with fish sauce, sugar and pepper.
Pour the boiling water over the tapioca starch, salt and 1 tbsp oil, stir, then add the cool water and knead into a smooth, soft dough.
Flatten small balls of dough into rounds, put a piece of pork and a shrimp on each, fold into a half moon and pinch shut.
Wrap each dumpling in a banana leaf square and steam 15 to 20 minutes, until the dough turns clear.
Serve warm with sweetened fish sauce.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the dried shrimp and pork.

recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham, Bánh Bột Lọc for every amount and step; 30 dumplings, same as ours.

recipes.name: Bánh Bèo
recipes.flavorProfile: Tiny, soft rice cakes steamed in saucers, topped with pink shrimp floss, crisp pork rind bits and scallion oil, eaten with a spoonful of dipping sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light, steamed rice snack; the shrimp topping brings protein, and the salted batter and shrimp make it fairly salty.
instructions: Whisk the rice flour, tapioca starch, water, salt and oil and let the batter rest at least 1 hour.
Oil small saucers, heat them in the steamer 2 minutes, then fill each with a thin layer of batter and steam 5 to 7 minutes until set and slightly hollow in the middle.
Cook the shrimp in a dry pan with 0.5 tsp salt and the pepper 4 to 5 minutes, then pound or pulse into fluffy floss.
Top each cake with shrimp floss, crushed pork rind and scallion oil.
Spoon a little dipping sauce over each cake and eat it straight from the saucer.
recipes.curationNote: Helen's Recipes, Bánh Bèo for every amount and step; serves 4 to 6, ours 6, same amounts.

recipes.name: Nem Nướng Cuốn
recipes.flavorProfile: Smoky, springy grilled pork sausage rolled in rice paper with crisp rice paper, green banana, star fruit, herbs and lettuce, dipped in a thick pâté and peanut sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Grilled pork brings protein and the raw fruit, herbs and greens bring fibre and vitamin C; the dipping sauce is rich, so a little goes far.

components.note: about 90 g worked into the dipping sauce

ingredients.cutPrep: boiled 5 minutes and cut in tiny dice
ingredients.prepNote: soaked in boiling water 10 minutes, drained and tossed with 1 tsp of the sugar
3 tsp in the pork, 1 tsp on the fat, 1 tsp in the sauce

ingredients.cutPrep: peeled and cut in thin strips
ingredients.prepNote: 1 each at 150 g per each; in place of green banana, which the database does not hold
2 tbsp colored with annatto for the pork, 2 tbsp for the sauce

ingredients.name: annatto seeds (hạt điều màu)
ingredients.prepNote: steeped in 2 tbsp of the oil and strained out

ingredients.baseName: Rice paper wrapper, soaked in water
ingredients.prepNote: 18 sheets, about 20 g each once dipped in water

instructions: Warm the annatto seeds in 2 tbsp of the oil over low heat until it turns red, then strain out the seeds.
Mix the pork with the 2 tbsp fish sauce, salt, 3 tsp sugar, pepper, starch, baking powder, shallot and the annatto oil. Rest 30 minutes, then chill.
Soak the diced fat in boiling water 10 minutes, drain, toss with 1 tsp sugar and fold into the pork.
With oiled hands, press the mixture onto soaked skewers and grill over hot coals 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.

For the sauce, fry the garlic in the remaining 2 tbsp oil, add the pâté, peanut butter and the water, then stir in the glutinous rice flour mixed with a little of the water and simmer until thick. Season with 1 tsp sugar and the 2 tbsp fish sauce and top with sesame seeds.
Roll each nem in a sheet of dampened rice paper with lettuce, mint, perilla, cucumber, banana, star fruit, pineapple and mango, and dip into the warm sauce.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the star fruit, pineapple, mango and herbs.
From the green banana, fruit and greens.

recipes.name: Thịt Kho Trứng (Caramelized Pork and Eggs)
recipes.flavorProfile: Meltingly soft pork belly and eggs braised in coconut water and caramel until glossy, sweet and salty, spooned over plain rice.
recipes.healthBenefit: Rich in protein from the pork and eggs, with B vitamins and choline from the eggs; the pork belly makes it a fatty, salty dish for the Tết table or a cold day.

components.note: steamed jasmine rice, about 1 cup per plate

ingredients.baseName: Gris sidfläsk bit rå m. svål

ingredients.prepNote: fresh coconut water (nước dừa); coconut soda is the common stand-in abroad

instructions: Blanch the pork in boiling water for 3 to 5 minutes, drain and rinse off the scum.
Put the pork in a heavy pot with the caramel, fish sauce, salt and onion and toss over medium heat 5 minutes until coated.
Add the coconut water and enough water to just cover, bring to a boil, skim, and simmer uncovered 1 to 1.5 hours.
Add the peeled eggs and simmer 30 to 45 minutes more, until the pork is tender and the eggs are amber.
Taste for salt, skim off some of the fat if you like, and serve with rice and pickled vegetables.
recipes.curationNote: Hungry Huy, Thịt Kho Trứng for every amount and step; serves 5: 2 lb pork half belly half shoulder, 3/4 cup coconut soda, 3 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tsp salt, water to cover, 4 tbsp nước màu, 8 eggs, 1 onion.

recipes.name: Cá Kho Tộ (Clay Pot Caramelized Fish)
recipes.flavorProfile: Catfish steaks simmered down in a clay pot with dark caramel and fish sauce until sticky, peppery and deeply savory, eaten with rice.
recipes.healthBenefit: Catfish brings protein, vitamin B12 and some omega-3 fats; the glaze is salty and sweet, so it is eaten in small amounts with lots of rice and vegetables.

components.note: steamed jasmine rice, about 1 cup per plate

ingredients.prepNote: 1 tbsp in the marinade, 2 tbsp for the caramel
fresh coconut water (nước dừa); coconut soda is the common stand-in abroad

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Marinate the catfish with the fish sauce and 1 tbsp sugar for at least 30 minutes.
In a clay pot or wide pan, heat the oil over medium high, add the remaining 2 tbsp sugar and cook until the caramel turns dark amber.
Stir in the shallot and garlic for about 15 seconds, then lay in the fish with its marinade and turn to coat.
Pour in the coconut water and simmer on low, partly covered, about 20 minutes, turning the fish or spooning the sauce over it halfway.
Top with the scallion and black pepper and serve in the pot with rice.
recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham, Cá Kho Tộ for every amount and step; serves 4: 3 lb catfish, 4 tbsp fish sauce, 3 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp oil, 1 shallot, 3 garlic, 6 oz coconut soda, 1 green onion, 1/4 tsp pepper; no chili.

recipes.name: Gà Kho Gừng (Ginger Braised Chicken)
recipes.flavorProfile: Bone-in chicken braised with a lot of ginger in caramel and fish sauce until sticky, warm and peppery.
recipes.healthBenefit: The chicken brings protein and niacin, and the generous ginger adds warmth and aroma; the sauce is salty, so the rice and greens alongside matter.

components.note: steamed jasmine rice, about 1 cup per plate

ingredients.cutPrep: bone in, chopped in 5 cm pieces

ingredients.prepNote: 2 tbsp in the marinade, 2 tbsp for the caramel
fresh coconut water (nước dừa); coconut soda is the common stand-in abroad

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)
Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Marinate the chicken with 2 tbsp sugar, the fish sauce and half the pepper for at least 30 minutes.
Cook the oil and remaining 2 tbsp sugar in a wide lidded pan over medium high until dark amber.
Add the ginger, garlic and shallot and fry about 30 seconds, then add the chicken and toss it in the caramel.
Pour in the coconut water, cover and simmer on low 10 minutes, tossing halfway, then uncover and cook about 10 minutes more until a little sauce is left.
Top with the rest of the pepper, cilantro, scallion and chili and serve with rice.
recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham, Gà Kho Gừng for every amount and step; serves 5: 3 lb chicken, 2 tbsp sugar, 3 tbsp fish sauce, 1/4 tsp pepper in the marinade; 1/4 cup ginger, 1 tbsp garlic, 2 tbsp shallot; caramel of 1 tbsp oil and 2 tbsp sugar; 1 cup coconut soda; 1/4 tsp pepper, 2 tbsp cilantro or green onion and optional chilies on top; bouillon left out.

recipes.name: Bò Lúc Lắc (Shaking Beef)
recipes.flavorProfile: Seared cubes of ribeye shaken in a hot wok with garlic and oyster sauce, tossed with onion and peppers, served with tomato rice and a lime pepper dip.
recipes.healthBenefit: A good share of protein, iron, zinc and vitamin B12 from the beef, with vitamin C from the peppers and tomato; ribeye makes it a rich plate.

components.note: cooked rice, fried with tomato paste

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

ingredients.prepNote: part of it infused with the garlic

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

ingredients.prepNote: two dashes, for the tomato rice

instructions: Toss the beef with oyster sauce, soy sauce, half the garlic, sugar and cornstarch and leave 30 minutes.
Fry the rest of the garlic in 2 tbsp oil until golden, strain it out and keep the garlic oil.
Fry the rice in a little garlic oil with the tomato paste and fish sauce 3 to 5 minutes until evenly red.
Heat a wok until smoking, add a little oil and the beef in one layer, sear 1 minute without moving, then shake the pan 1 to 2 minutes for medium rare. Lift out.
Stir-fry the onion, pepper and scallion 1 minute, return the beef and the garlic oil and toss.
Serve on lettuce and tomato with the tomato rice and the salt, pepper and lime dip.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the bell pepper and tomato.

recipes.curationNote: Hungry Huy, Bò Lúc Lắc for every amount and step; serves 2: 1 lb ribeye, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp soy, garlic, 2 tbsp garlic oil, 1/2 tsp sugar, 1 tsp starch; tomato rice with 1 tbsp tomato paste and two dashes fish sauce; onion, bell pepper, green onion; lime, salt and pepper dip.

recipes.name: Bò Kho (Beef Stew)
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender beef shank and carrots in a red, aromatic broth of lemongrass, star anise and tomato, eaten with crusty bread or noodles and Thai basil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef shank brings protein, collagen, iron and zinc, and the carrots add vitamin A; a warming, filling stew.

components.note: one roll per bowl, for dipping
1 tsp, or bò kho spice mix

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

ingredients.cutPrep: stalks bruised and cut in 10 cm lengths

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
ingredients.prepNote: 2 tbsp at 16 g per tbsp; in place of dark soy sauce, which the database does not hold
fresh coconut water (nước dừa); coconut soda is the common stand-in abroad
in place of Thai basil leaves (húng quế), which the database does not hold

instructions: Toss the beef with salt, soy sauce, hoisin, half the garlic, paprika and curry powder and marinate at least 1 hour.
Brown the beef in the oil in batches, 5 to 7 minutes, then fry the onion, ginger, the rest of the garlic and the lemongrass 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, dark soy, star anise and bay leaves, return the beef, and add the broth, coconut water and water.
Simmer covered 1.5 to 2 hours, until the beef is tender.
Add the carrots and simmer 20 to 30 minutes more, until soft. Take out the lemongrass, anise and bay.
Serve with Thai basil and warm bánh mì, or over rice noodles.

recipes.name: Gà Xào Sả Ớt (Lemongrass Chili Chicken)
recipes.flavorProfile: Bite-size chicken stir-fried with a heap of fragrant lemongrass, garlic and chili until golden and slightly sticky, salty sweet and hot.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lean protein from the chicken with the aroma of lemongrass and chili; a quick weeknight dish to pair with rice and greens.

components.note: steamed jasmine rice, about 1 cup per plate

ingredients.cutPrep: boned and cut in bite-size pieces

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Marinate the chicken with half the lemongrass, half the garlic, the fish sauce, sugar, chili and salt for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oil on high and fry the rest of the lemongrass and garlic until fragrant, then add the chicken and stir until no longer pink.
Cover and cook on medium 5 to 10 minutes, then uncover and stir 2 to 3 minutes more.
Add the onion and stir 1 to 2 minutes, until translucent.
Serve hot with rice.

recipes.name: Tôm Rim (Caramelized Shrimp)
recipes.flavorProfile: Small shrimp simmered in fish sauce and sugar until lacquered, sweet, salty and peppery, a little goes a long way over rice.
recipes.healthBenefit: Shrimp bring protein, selenium and vitamin B12; the glaze is salty, so it is eaten a few at a time with plain rice and soup.

components.note: steamed jasmine rice, about 1 cup per plate

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Marinate the shrimp with the fish sauce, sugar, half the pepper and half the garlic and shallot for at least 15 minutes.
Heat the oil over medium-high heat and fry the rest of the garlic and shallot with the scallion whites for about 15 seconds.
Add the shrimp and marinade, cover and simmer 2 minutes, then uncover and cook over medium about 8 minutes, until the liquid is gone and the shells are shiny.
Top with the scallion greens and the rest of the pepper and serve with rice.
recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham, Tôm Rim for every amount and step; serves 8: 2 lb small shrimp, 3 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp bouillon powder, 1 1/2 tbsp sugar, 1/2 tsp pepper divided, optional MSG, 2 tbsp garlic and 3 tbsp shallot each half in the marinade, 2 tbsp oil, 1 green onion; salt rubbed on and rinsed off.

recipes.name: Sườn Ram Mặn (Caramelized Pork Ribs)
recipes.flavorProfile: Short pieces of spare rib blanched, then braised in caramel, fish sauce and coconut water until the meat is tender and the glaze is dark and sticky.
recipes.healthBenefit: The ribs bring protein, zinc and B vitamins; they are fatty and the glaze is salty sweet, so serve with plenty of rice and vegetables.

components.note: steamed jasmine rice, about 1 cup per plate

ingredients.prepNote: 1 tbsp in the marinade, 2 tbsp for the caramel
fresh coconut water (nước dừa); coconut soda is the common stand-in abroad

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Blanch the ribs in boiling water for about 8 minutes, drain and rinse.
Toss the ribs with shallot, garlic, fish sauce, pepper and 1 tbsp sugar and leave 20 minutes.
Melt the remaining 2 tbsp sugar in a heavy pan over medium heat 3 to 5 minutes into an amber caramel, add the ribs and turn to coat.
Add the coconut water and water and braise uncovered 30 to 40 minutes, turning, until the sauce is a thick glaze.
Top with scallion and serve with rice.
recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham, Sườn Ram Mặn for every amount and step; serves 3: 2 lb ribs, 1 shallot, 3 garlic, 1 tbsp bouillon powder, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1/2 tsp pepper, 3 tbsp sugar divided, 3/4 cup coconut soda, 1/2 cup water, 1 green onion, 1 tsp salt in the blanching water.

recipes.name: Chả Cá Lã Vọng (Turmeric Fish with Dill)
recipes.flavorProfile: Golden turmeric and galangal fish sizzled with heaps of dill and spring onion, eaten over rice noodles with herbs, peanuts and a pungent shrimp paste dip.
recipes.healthBenefit: White fish brings lean protein and the big handfuls of dill and spring onion add greens; the shrimp paste dip is salty, so use it sparingly.

components.note: 1 tbsp, plain yogurt is the usual stand-in

ingredients.prepNote: (1 tsp for the marinade, 2 tbsp for the dip; 7 tsp at 6 g per tsp)
(1 tbsp for the marinade, 1 tbsp for the dip, the rest for frying)

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)
Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Marinate the fish with turmeric, galangal, rice flour, mẻ, 1 tsp shrimp paste, 1 tbsp oil and pepper for at least 1 hour.
Bake the fish on an oiled tray at 400°F (200°C) for 5 to 7 minutes until just set.
For the dip, stir 2 tbsp shrimp paste with the sugar, lime juice, garlic and chili until it foams, then stir in 1 tbsp hot oil.
Heat the rest of the oil in a skillet at the table or stove, fry the fish 2 to 3 minutes until golden, then pile on the spring onion and dill and toss 1 minute until just wilted.
Spoon fish and greens over bowls of bún, add peanuts, shiso and basil, and drizzle with the shrimp paste dip.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the dill and spring onion.

citations.source: Helen's Recipes, Chả Cá Lã Vọng

Amounts kept as given; the page says 2 to 3 servings.

recipes.name: Bò Nướng Lá Lốt (Beef in Betel Leaves)
recipes.flavorProfile: Little cigars of curry-scented ground beef wrapped in peppery wild betel leaves and grilled until smoky, eaten with lettuce, pickles and nước chấm.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef brings protein, iron and zinc and the leaves and pickles add greens and crunch; a light grilled dish when eaten with herbs.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

ingredients.prepNote: club soda, to keep the filling moist

instructions: Mix the beef with scallion, fish sauce, salt, pepper, curry powder and the club soda and rest 15 minutes.
Lay a leaf shiny side down, put a heaped teaspoon of beef at the stem end, roll it into a short log and set seam down.
Thread the rolls onto skewers or set them in a grill basket and brush lightly with oil.
Grill over medium hot coals or under a broiler 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until the leaves char a little and the beef is cooked.
Serve with lettuce, mint, pickles and nước chấm.

recipes.curationNote: Viet World Kitchen, Beef in Wild Betel Leaf (Bò Lá Lốt) for every amount and step; 1 lb beef, 1/4 cup green onion, 2 tsp fish sauce, scant 1/2 tsp salt, 3/4 tsp pepper, 2 to 3 tsp curry powder, 1 to 2 tbsp club soda, 115 g leaves, 1 tbsp oil, lettuce.

recipes.name: Chạo Tôm (Shrimp on Sugarcane)
recipes.flavorProfile: Bouncy shrimp paste moulded around sticks of sugarcane, steamed then grilled until smoky, with sweet juice to chew from the cane after.
recipes.healthBenefit: Shrimp bring protein and selenium; served wrapped in lettuce and herbs, it is a light grilled starter.

ingredients.name: sugarcane sticks
ingredients.cutPrep: cut 10 cm long and split in quarters
ingredients.prepNote: for the skewers; chewed but not eaten

instructions: Pulse the shrimp with salt, cornstarch, sugar, pepper, fish sauce, egg, garlic and shallot into a sticky paste, then fold in the diced fat. Chill 30 minutes.
With wet hands, flatten about 2 tbsp of paste into a round, set a stick on it and wrap the paste around the middle, smoothing it.
Steam the sticks 3 to 4 minutes until the paste is opaque and set.
Brush with oil and grill over medium coals 5 to 7 minutes, turning, until golden and charred in spots.
Slide the shrimp off and wrap in lettuce with mint, cilantro and perilla, dip in nước chấm, then chew the cane.
recipes.curationNote: Viet World Kitchen, Chạo Tôm for every amount and step; makes 12: 1 lb shrimp, generous 1/4 tsp salt, 2 tsp cornstarch, 2 tsp palm or light brown sugar, generous 1/4 tsp pepper, 2 tsp fish sauce, 1 egg, 2 garlic, 2 tbsp shallot, 1 tbsp fatback; 1 to 2 tbsp oil; lettuce, cilantro, mint and perilla.

recipes.name: Gà Nướng Sả (Lemongrass Grilled Chicken)
recipes.flavorProfile: Chicken thighs marinated in lemongrass, garlic, honey, oyster and soy sauces and a little five-spice, grilled until charred and juicy, served with rice, cucumber, tomato and pickles.
recipes.healthBenefit: Grilled chicken brings protein and niacin with little added fat; serve with pickles and greens for a balanced plate.

components.note: steamed jasmine rice, about 1 cup per plate

instructions: Stir the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, honey, sugar, Shaoxing wine, five-spice, pepper, garlic and lemongrass together.
Coat the chicken and marinate at least 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge.

Grill at about 400°F (200°C), skin side down first, 10 minutes a side (12 for bone-in), until 165°F (74°C) inside. To roast instead, cook skin side down on a rack at 400°F (200°C) 15 minutes, turn and cook 15 minutes more, then baste with the drippings and broil 1 to 2 minutes a side until crisp.
Serve over rice with cucumber, tomato and pickles.

recipes.name: Mực Xào (Stir-Fried Squid)
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender scored squid tossed fast over high heat with celery, cucumber, pineapple, tomato and onion, bright, sweet and a little sour.
recipes.healthBenefit: Squid brings lean protein, copper and vitamin B12, and the vegetables and pineapple add vitamin C.

components.note: steamed jasmine rice, about 1 cup per plate

ingredients.cutPrep: cleaned, scored and cut in pieces

ingredients.prepNote: Chinese celery is the usual choice

instructions: Blanch the squid in boiling water for 15 to 20 seconds and drain well, so it stays tender in the wok.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and fry the garlic 30 seconds.
Add the onion, celery and cucumber and stir-fry 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the pineapple, tomato, squid, fish sauce and sugar and toss 1 to 2 minutes, just until hot.
Serve right away with rice.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pineapple, tomato and vegetables.

recipes.name: Đậu Hũ Sốt Cà Chua (Tofu in Tomato Sauce)
recipes.flavorProfile: Golden fried tofu with a soft centre simmered in a sweet, savory fresh tomato sauce with scallion, simple and comforting over rice.
recipes.healthBenefit: Tofu brings plant protein and calcium, and the tomatoes lycopene and vitamin C; fish sauce can be swapped for soy sauce to make it plant based.

components.note: steamed jasmine rice, about 1 cup per plate

ingredients.cutPrep: firm, cut in 3 cm cubes and patted dry

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Shallow fry the tofu in the oil over medium high 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until golden on all sides. Drain.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp oil and cook the tomatoes and the white parts of the scallion 5 to 7 minutes until broken down.
Stir in the tomato paste, fish sauce, salt, sugar and water and simmer 3 to 5 minutes.
Add the tofu and simmer 5 minutes so it takes in the sauce.
Scatter the green scallion over and serve with rice.

nutritionHighlights.note: From tofu set with calcium salts.

recipes.name: Canh Chua Cá (Sour Fish Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: A clear, sweet and sour tamarind broth full of fish, pineapple, tomato, okra and bean sprouts, sharp with herbs and garlic.
recipes.healthBenefit: Fish brings protein and the vegetables and pineapple add vitamin C and fibre; a light, brothy soup that fills the table with vegetables.

components.note: steamed rice eaten with the soup

ingredients.cutPrep: pulp soaked in hot water and strained
peeled and sliced on the angle

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Fry the garlic in the oil until golden, lift it out for the top and keep the oil in the pot.
Sear the fish in the garlic oil about 10 seconds a side, pour in the water, bring to a boil and simmer gently 15 minutes, skimming.
Dissolve the tamarind in a cup of the hot broth, strain it back into the pot, and season with the fish sauce, salt and sugar; it should taste bold.
Add the pineapple, tomato, okra and taro stem, bring back to a simmer, then turn off the heat.
Add the bean sprouts and finish each bowl with the herbs, fried garlic and chili. Serve with rice.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pineapple, tomato and okra.

recipes.name: Canh Bí Đao (Winter Melon Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: A gentle, clear soup of translucent winter melon and sweet minced shrimp, light and cooling.
recipes.healthBenefit: Winter melon is mostly water with a little vitamin C, and the shrimp add protein and selenium; a light, low-fat soup for an everyday meal.

components.note: steamed rice eaten with the soup

ingredients.cutPrep: peeled, seeded and cut in thin pieces

ingredients.prepNote: 1.5 g for the shrimp, 3 g for the soup

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Pound the shrimp with half the shallot and 1.5 g salt, then mix in the fish sauce and pepper.
Fry the rest of the shallot in the oil until fragrant, add the shrimp and stir over high heat until they turn orange.
Pour in the 1 litre of hot water, add the remaining 3 g salt and the winter melon, and bring back to a boil; turn off the heat once it boils.
Finish with scallion and cilantro and serve with rice.

recipes.name: Canh Cải Thịt Bằm (Mustard Greens and Pork Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: A simple clear broth with stir-fried minced pork, wood ear and peppery mustard greens, with a slight bitterness and black pepper warmth.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mustard greens bring vitamins A, C and K and calcium, and the pork adds protein; an everyday soup that puts greens on the table.

components.note: steamed rice eaten with the soup

ingredients.cutPrep: stalks and leaves apart, bite-size pieces

ingredients.baseName: Mushrooms, tree ears, Cloud ear, dried

instructions: Wash the mustard greens, keep the stalks and leaves apart and cut them in bite-size pieces. Chop the soaked wood ear and mix it into the ground pork.
Heat the oil in a pot and fry the shallot until fragrant. Add the pork and wood ear and stir-fry until it changes colour, then add the water and bring to a boil.
Add the mustard green stalks and cook 2 minutes.
Add the leaves and the salt and cook 1 to 2 minutes more. Sprinkle with pepper, take off the heat and serve with rice.

recipes.name: Canh Rau Ngót (Sweet Leaf Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, dark green sweet leaves in a clear pork broth, mild, sweet and grassy.
recipes.healthBenefit: Sweet leaf is a leafy green with vitamin C and carotenes, and the pork adds protein; a light home soup served with rice.

components.note: steamed rice eaten with the soup

ingredients.name: sweet leaf (rau ngót, Sauropus androgynus)
ingredients.cutPrep: leaves stripped, bruised and roughly chopped

instructions: Fry the garlic and shallot in the oil about 20 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook until lightly browned, breaking it up.
Pour in the 4 cups of water, bring to a gentle boil and simmer about 10 minutes, skimming.
Season with the fish sauce, salt, sugar and pepper, tasting as you go.
Add the sweet leaves a handful at a time and cook about 8 minutes, until tender. Serve with rice.

recipes.name: Súp Cua (Crab Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: A thick, silky crab soup with ribbons of egg, quail eggs, asparagus and mushrooms, finished with pepper and cilantro.
recipes.healthBenefit: Crab and eggs bring protein, zinc and vitamin B12; the tapioca thickening makes it a starchy, comforting starter.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Bring the broth to a boil, add the crab and mushrooms and simmer 5 minutes. Taste and add the salt only if it needs it.
Add the quail eggs, then slowly pour in the beaten egg while stirring in one direction to make ribbons.
Stir in the tapioca slurry and simmer until the soup thickens and coats a spoon.
Turn off the heat and add the asparagus to cook in the heat of the soup.
Ladle into bowls and finish with sesame oil, white pepper, cilantro and scallion.

recipes.name: Canh Khổ Qua Nhồi Thịt (Stuffed Bitter Melon Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: Rings of bitter melon packed with peppery pork, wood ear and glass noodles, simmered soft in a clear broth, bitter, savory and soothing.
recipes.healthBenefit: Bitter melon brings vitamin C and fibre and the pork brings protein; the soup is eaten on Tết to let hard times pass, with rice on the side.

components.note: steamed rice eaten with the soup

ingredients.cutPrep: cut in 5 cm rings and seeded

ingredients.baseName: Mushrooms, tree ears, Cloud ear, dried
Glass noodles made from mung bean starch
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Mix the pork, wood ear, glass noodles, onion, fish sauce, sugar, salt and pepper.
Slit or split the bitter melons, scoop out the seeds and pack them firmly with the filling.
Bring the stock and water to a boil, lower in the stuffed melons and skim.
Simmer gently 20 to 30 minutes, until the melon is fork tender, then taste the broth and thin it with a little hot water if it is too strong.
Cut the melons into pieces and serve in the broth with scallion and cilantro.

recipes.name: Lẩu Cá (Fish Hot Pot)
recipes.flavorProfile: A tamarind and pineapple sour broth kept bubbling at the table, with fish, tomato, mushrooms and greens cooked in it a little at a time and eaten over rice noodles.
recipes.healthBenefit: Fish brings protein and the greens, tomato and pineapple add vitamin C and fibre; a shared meal heavy on vegetables.

ingredients.cutPrep: in pieces; the source uses snakehead (cá lóc), which is in neither database, so catfish stands in
soaked in hot water and strained for its sour liquid
cooked; the source says bún or rice without an amount
bạc hà stalks, peeled and sliced

instructions: Rinse the fish and cut it in pieces. Strain the tamarind for its sour liquid. Blend half the pineapple and slice the rest. Clean the vegetables and chop the herbs.

Cook the fish in the broth until done and lift it out. Add half the herbs and the fried garlic to the broth, set the fish on a plate and scatter the rest of the herbs over with the remaining tomato and pineapple.

At the table, bring the broth back to a boil, warm the fish in it and cook the okra, bạc hà, water spinach, mushrooms and bean sprouts as you go. Eat with the noodles and plain fish sauce for dipping.

recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, sweet slivers of bottle gourd in a clear broth sweetened by dried shrimp fried with garlic, mild and summery.
recipes.healthBenefit: The gourd is light and watery with a little vitamin C, and the shrimp add protein and calcium; a simple, low-fat soup.

components.note: steamed rice eaten with the soup

ingredients.baseName: Crustacean, processed shrimp, boiled and dried shrimp
ingredients.prepNote: (1/2 cup) soaked 5 minutes, rinsed and drained

recipes.name: Gỏi Gà Bắp Cải (Chicken and Cabbage Salad)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp shredded cabbage, carrot and onion tossed with poached chicken, rau răm and a lime fish sauce dressing, crunchy and peppery.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lean chicken brings protein and the cabbage, carrot and herbs bring vitamins C and K and fibre; a fresh, light main salad.

ingredients.cutPrep: very thinly sliced and soaked in cold water

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

Soak the sliced onion in cold water 10 minutes and drain.

recipes.name: Gỏi Đu Đủ (Green Papaya Salad)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crunchy strands of green papaya with chewy sweet beef jerky and Thai basil in a sweet, sour and salty soy dressing with chile, the Sài Gòn street snack.
recipes.healthBenefit: Green papaya brings vitamin C and fibre and the herbs add freshness; the jerky makes it salty and sweet, so it is a snack portion.

ingredients.cutPrep: green, peeled, seeded and finely shredded

ingredients.prepNote: in place of Thai basil leaves (húng quế), which the database does not hold

ingredients.cutPrep: 1 tsp for the papaya, 2 tbsp for the dressing

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green
Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

recipes.name: Nộm Hoa Chuối (Banana Blossom Salad)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fine shreds of crisp, slightly astringent banana blossom with pork, shrimp, herbs and peanuts in a sweet lime dressing.
recipes.healthBenefit: Banana blossom brings fibre and the pork and shrimp bring protein; a bright, crunchy salad for a shared table.

components.note: about 6 tbsp to dress the salad

ingredients.name: banana blossom
ingredients.cutPrep: outer bracts removed, finely shredded into lime water

ingredients.name: lime juice, for the soaking water
ingredients.prepNote: in the water the sliced banana blossom waits in, poured away, not eaten

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Shred the banana blossom straight into water with lime juice so it does not darken, soak 15 minutes, then drain and squeeze dry.
Season the pork and the shrimp separately with the shallot, pepper and a spoonful of the nước chấm.
Stir-fry the pork in a little of the oil from the fried shallots for about 3 minutes, then add the shrimp and cook over high heat until pink.
Toss the blossom, carrot, mint, pork and shrimp with the rest of the nước chấm.
Top with peanuts, fried shallots and chili.
recipes.curationNote: Helen's Recipes, Nộm Hoa Chuối for every amount and step; serves 4: 200 g banana blossom, 100 g carrot, 200 g pork, 200 g shrimp, 1/2 cup mint, 10 g shallot and pepper for the proteins, which are stir-fried; dressing of garlic, chili, sugar, fish sauce and lime; fried shallot and peanuts; no rau răm.

recipes.name: Gỏi Ngó Sen (Lotus Stem Salad)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp, pale lotus stems with shrimp, carrot, cucumber and rau răm in a sweet and sour dressing, scooped up with prawn crackers at parties.
recipes.healthBenefit: The shrimp brings protein and the lotus stems and carrot add crunch and fibre; a festive salad.

components.note: about 8 tbsp to dress the salad
450 g, rinsed, drained and halved lengthwise

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Rinse and drain the lotus stems and squeeze gently.
Boil the shrimp 2 to 3 minutes, until pink, and halve them lengthwise.
Toss the lotus stems, carrot, cucumber, shrimp and rau răm with the nước chấm.
Top with peanuts, fried shallots and chili. Serve with prawn crackers if you like.

citations.source: Vicky Pham, Lotus Root Shrimp Salad

recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham, Lotus Root Shrimp Salad for every amount and step; serves 5, scaled to our 6: 16 oz lotus in brine, 1 lb shrimp, a handful of rau răm, 1/4 cup peanuts, 1/4 cup fried shallots, red onion; dressing of fish sauce, lime, sugar, garlic and chili; carrot or cucumber mentioned as options; no pork or mint.

recipes.name: Rau Muống Xào Tỏi (Garlic Water Spinach)
recipes.flavorProfile: Hollow, crunchy water spinach stems flashed in a hot wok with a lot of garlic and a little oyster sauce, green, garlicky and savory.
recipes.healthBenefit: Water spinach brings vitamins A and C, iron and fibre; a fast way to put a big plate of greens on the table.

ingredients.cutPrep: cut in 12 cm lengths, shoots and leaves kept apart

instructions: Trim the rough ends, cut the water spinach into lengths and keep the shoots and leaves apart.
Bring a wok half full of water to the boil with the salt. Blanch the shoots no more than 1 minute and the leaves no more than 30 seconds, cool them in iced water and drain well.
Mix the oyster sauce and sugar in a small bowl.
Dry the wok, heat the oil and fry the garlic until fragrant.
Add the water spinach and the oyster sauce mixture and toss lightly until coated. Serve right away with rice.

citations.source: Vicky Pham, Stir-Fried Water Spinach with Beef (Rau Muống Xào Thịt Bò)

recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham, Stir-Fried Water Spinach with Beef (Rau Muống Xào Thịt Bò), garlic-only version for every amount and step; the page says the beef can be left out for a garlic and oyster sauce version; the water spinach part is 3 lb water spinach, 1 tsp salt in the blanching water, oil, 6 garlic cloves, 3 tbsp oyster sauce, 3 tsp sugar; blanched shoots 1 minute, leaves 30 seconds, iced; the final toss uses 2 tbsp oil.

recipes.name: Cà Tím Nướng Mỡ Hành (Grilled Eggplant with Scallion Oil)
recipes.flavorProfile: Smoky, soft grilled eggplant pulled into strips and covered with a sweet garlic and chili fish sauce, hot scallion oil, fried shallots and peanuts.
recipes.healthBenefit: Eggplant brings fibre and the scallion oil adds flavor; a light vegetable side.

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

ingredients.cutPrep: 2 tbsp for the fish sauce, 1 tsp crushed with the garlic

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Prick the eggplants all over and grill them whole over charcoal or a gas flame 15 to 20 minutes, turning often, until the skin is charred and a toothpick goes in easily. Peel off the skin.
Crush the garlic, chili and 1 tsp sugar in a mortar. Stir the remaining 2 tbsp sugar into the fish sauce until dissolved, then add the crushed garlic and chili.
Heat the oil until it smokes and pour it over the chopped green onion.
Pick off any black bits, pull the eggplant flesh into thin strips with a fork and lay it on a plate. Spoon the sauce over, top with the scallion oil and scatter with fried shallots and peanuts.

citations.source: Helen's Recipes, Cà Tím Nướng Mỡ Hành

recipes.curationNote: Helen's Recipes, Cà Tím Nướng Mỡ Hành for every amount and step; 3 eggplants grilled 15 to 20 minutes; sauce of 2 to 3 garlic cloves, 1 small chili and 1 tsp sugar crushed, stirred into 3 tbsp fish sauce with 2 tbsp sugar; scallion oil of 1 bunch green onion and 2 to 3 tbsp smoking hot oil; fried shallots and peanuts optional with no amounts.

recipes.name: Rau Củ Luộc Chấm Kho Quẹt (Boiled Vegetables with Caramelized Fish Sauce Dip)
recipes.flavorProfile: Plain boiled vegetables dragged through a thick, sticky dip of caramelized fish sauce, crisp pork fat and pepper, salty, sweet and deeply savory.
recipes.healthBenefit: A big plate of vegetables brings fibre and vitamins; the kho quẹt dip is salty and rich, so a little goes on each bite.

ingredients.baseName: Crustacean, processed shrimp, boiled and dried shrimp

ingredients.prepNote: some in the dip, some over the top

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Stir the fish sauce and sugar together until the sugar dissolves.
Render the diced pork fat in a small clay pot or heavy pan over medium-high heat until crisp, then lift out the cracklings.
Fry the shallot and garlic in the fat until fragrant, then add the dried shrimp and pork and stir-fry until the pork is no longer pink.

Add the fish sauce mixture, the chilies and most of the pepper, and simmer uncovered over medium-low heat about 20 minutes, until thick and caramelized. Top with the cracklings and the rest of the pepper.
Boil the okra 4 to 5 minutes and blanch the cauliflower, carrot and zucchini 1 to 2 minutes each. Serve them around the pot with rice.
recipes.curationNote: Helen's Recipes, Mắm Kho Quẹt for every amount and step; serves 4: 3 tbsp fish sauce, 3 tbsp sugar, optional stock, 2 tbsp diced pork fat, 1 shallot, 3 garlic, 3 tbsp dried shrimp, 30 g lean pork, 3 to 4 bird's eye chilies, pepper to taste; no water or caramel; vegetables: 1 small cauliflower or broccoli, 1 daikon, carrot or bitter melon, 1 opo squash or zucchini, 200 g okra.

recipes.name: Đậu Que Xào Tỏi (Garlic Green Beans)
recipes.flavorProfile: Snappy green beans, blanched and then tossed in olive oil with plenty of fried garlic, salt and pepper.
recipes.healthBenefit: Green beans bring fibre, vitamin C and vitamin K; a quick, light vegetable side.

ingredients.cutPrep: trimmed and cut in 5 cm lengths

instructions: Blanch the beans in boiling salted water about 3 minutes, until bright green but still firm, then rinse under cold water and drain.
Heat the oil over medium heat and fry the sliced garlic about 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the beans and toss about 2 minutes, until just tender.
Season with the salt and pepper and serve.

citations.source: Hungry Huy, Garlic Sautéed Green Beans

recipes.curationNote: Hungry Huy, Garlic Sautéed Green Beans for every amount and step; serves 3: 1/2 lb green beans blanched in salted water, 1 tbsp butter or olive oil, 6 garlic cloves, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/8 tsp pepper.

recipes.name: Bò Tái Chanh (Lime-Cured Beef Salad)
recipes.flavorProfile: Paper-thin slices of beef turned pale and tender in lime juice, tossed with onion, herbs, peanuts and fried shallots, sharp and fresh.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lean beef brings protein, iron and vitamin B12 and the lime and herbs add vitamin C; the beef is cured, not cooked, so it needs very fresh meat.

ingredients.cutPrep: partly frozen and sliced paper thin

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Soak the sliced onion in ice water 10 minutes, drain, and toss with 2 tablespoons of the sugar and the vinegar.
Toss the sliced beef in the lime juice and leave 10 to 15 minutes, turning, until most of it turns pale. Squeeze the beef firmly to press out the juice.
Toss the beef with the garlic, the last tablespoon of sugar, the salt and pepper, then mix in the drained onion and the chili.
Fold in the mint, rice paddy herb and culantro, top with peanuts and fried shallots, and serve with nước chấm for dipping.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the lime juice and herbs.

recipes.curationNote: Helen's Recipes, Bò Tái Chanh for every amount and step; serves 4 to 6: 500 g beef, 2 onions, 4 limes, 1 knob garlic, 2 chilies, 3 tbsp sugar, 3 tbsp vinegar, about 1/2 tsp each salt, pepper and stock powder, mint, rice paddy herb, sawtooth coriander, fried shallot, peanuts, fish sauce dip.

recipes.name: Dưa Giá (Pickled Bean Sprouts)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crunchy, sour bean sprouts with chives, carrot, chili and ginger, pickled a day or two in a sweet vinegar brine, the bright side for thịt kho at Tết.
recipes.healthBenefit: A quick vinegar pickle with vitamin C and fibre; it cuts the richness of braised pork, and the brine carries sugar and some salt.
instructions: Stir the water, vinegar, sugar and salt together until dissolved.
Toss the bean sprouts, chives, carrot, chili and ginger in a large bowl, pour the brine over and leave 1 to 2 hours, until the sprouts wilt.
Pack into a clean jar, keeping the vegetables under the brine, and keep somewhere cool.
Eat after 1 to 2 days; it keeps 1 to 2 weeks in the fridge.
recipes.curationNote: Helen's Recipes, Dưa Giá for every amount and step; serves 4 to 6: 500 g bean sprouts, 100 g garlic chives, 1 carrot, 2 red chilies, a thumb of ginger, 1 cup water, 1 cup white vinegar, 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 tsp salt. Amounts kept as given for the same 500 g of sprouts.

recipes.name: Chè Ba Màu (Three-Color Dessert)
recipes.flavorProfile: Layers of sweet red beans, smooth yellow mung bean paste and green pandan jelly under crushed ice and salty sweet coconut cream.
recipes.healthBenefit: The beans bring plant protein, fibre and folate; the sugar and coconut cream make it a sweet treat for a hot afternoon.

ingredients.baseName: Kidney beans, mature seeds, "Koshi-an" (strained sweet bean paste)
ingredients.cutPrep: canned sweetened red bean paste, 1 1/2 cans
ingredients.prepNote: red beans, as in the south; adzuki also used

ingredients.cutPrep: split and peeled, soaked at least 4 hours
4 1/2 tbsp for the mung beans, 4 1/2 tbsp for the jelly, 3 tbsp for the sauce
ingredients.prepNote: divided between the beans, mung paste and jelly

ingredients.cutPrep: 270 ml for the mung beans, 720 ml for the jelly

instructions: Soak the mung beans at least 4 hours or overnight and drain. Cook them with 270 ml water in a rice cooker on the regular setting, or simmer about 40 minutes, until soft. Mash, stir in 4 1/2 tbsp sugar and chill.

Bring 720 ml water to a boil and dissolve the agar and 4 1/2 tbsp sugar in it. Lower the heat, stir in the pandan extract and pour into a glass dish. Cool, chill about 2 hours until firm and cut in strips.
Heat the coconut cream, 3 tbsp sugar and salt over medium heat, whisk in the starch and cook 1 to 2 minutes until it thickens like a thin pudding. Cool and chill.
In each tall glass layer shaved ice, red bean paste, mung beans, pandan jelly and more ice, and top with the coconut sauce. Stir before eating.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the red beans and mung beans.
From the syrup in each layer.

recipes.curationNote: Hungry Huy, Chè Ba Màu for every amount and step; serves 4, scaled x1.5 to our 6: 1/2 cup split mung beans soaked, cooked in 3/4 cup water, mashed with 3 tbsp sugar; jelly of 1 tbsp agar powder, 2 cups water, 1/4 tsp pandan extract, 3 tbsp sugar; 1 can (16.75 oz) boiled red bean paste; sauce of 7 oz coconut cream, 2 tbsp sugar, 1/3 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp tapioca starch; 4 cups shaved ice.

recipes.name: Chè Chuối (Banana and Tapioca Pudding)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, sweet banana chunks and chewy tapioca pearls in warm salty sweet coconut cream, scattered with toasted sesame and peanuts.
recipes.healthBenefit: Bananas bring potassium and the coconut cream makes it rich; a warm sweet treat.

ingredients.prepNote: chuối sứ (Thai banana) is used in Việt Nam
1.8 g in the pudding, 3.6 g in the topping

instructions: Soak the tapioca pearls in warm water about 20 minutes and drain.
Slice the bananas, coat them with the sugar and chill at least 30 minutes.
Boil the water with the knotted pandan leaves and simmer about 20 minutes.
Add the bananas with their sugar, the coconut cream, tapioca and 1.8 g salt, and simmer 15 to 20 minutes until the bananas are soft.
Mix the peanuts and sesame with the remaining salt and sprinkle over each bowl, warm or chilled.
recipes.curationNote: Hungry Huy, Chè Chuối for every amount and step; serves 5, scaled to our 6: 1 lb bananas, 3 tbsp small tapioca, 4 oz sugar, 2 cups water, 4 pandan leaves, 1/2 can coconut cream, 1/4 tsp salt; topping of 2 tbsp peanuts, 2 tbsp sesame, 1/2 tsp salt.

recipes.name: Chè Đậu Xanh (Mung Bean Pudding)
recipes.flavorProfile: Whole mung beans simmered soft with red dates, sweetened with sugar and finished with coconut milk and vanilla, eaten warm, chilled or over ice.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mung beans bring plant protein, fibre and folate; it is sweetened, so it is a dessert portion.
instructions: Rinse the mung beans until the water runs clear and drain. Snip the red dates.

Put the beans, dates and water in a pot, bring to a boil and skim the foam. Simmer partly covered about 40 minutes, until the beans smash easily but keep a little bite (20 to 25 minutes if soaked 4 hours first). Take out the dates.
Stir in the rock sugar, salt, vanilla and coconut milk and simmer on low 5 minutes.
Serve warm, chilled or over crushed ice.

citations.source: Vicky Pham, Chè Đậu Xanh (Vietnamese Mung Bean Dessert with Coconut Milk)

recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham, Chè Đậu Xanh (Vietnamese Mung Bean Dessert with Coconut Milk) for every amount and step; serves 6: 1 cup whole green mung beans, 9 cups water, 1 cup dried red dates, 1/4 cup sago optional, 3.5 oz yellow rock sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp vanilla, 1 cup coconut milk.

recipes.name: Bánh Flan (Caramel Custard)
recipes.flavorProfile: Smooth, silky custard of eggs, coconut cream, milk and condensed milk under a bitter dark caramel, often with a splash of black coffee over the top.
recipes.healthBenefit: Eggs bring protein, choline and vitamin B12; with condensed milk and caramel it is a rich, sweet treat.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Butter 8 ramekins. Cook the sugar and water over medium heat 5 to 8 minutes into a dark amber caramel, stir in the lime juice and pour a thin layer into each ramekin.
Warm the coconut cream, milk and condensed milk until steaming, not boiling.
Whisk the eggs and yolks gently without making foam, then slowly whisk in the warm milk and vanilla, and strain.
Pour into the ramekins, cover each, and steam over gentle heat 20 to 25 minutes, or bake in a water bath at 325°F (160°C) for 35 to 40 minutes, until just set.
Chill at least 4 hours, run a knife round and turn out. Serve with crushed ice and a little black coffee if you like.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the condensed milk and caramel.

recipes.curationNote: Helen's Recipes, Bánh Flan Dừa for every amount and step; makes 10 small moulds; ours fills 8 ramekins with the same batch.

recipes.name: Bánh Chuối Nướng (Baked Banana Cake)
recipes.flavorProfile: A dense, moist, pudding-like cake of ripe bananas and bread soaked in coconut milk and condensed milk, caramelized on top and served chilled.
recipes.healthBenefit: Bananas bring potassium; with sugar, condensed milk, butter and bread it is a sweet treat.

ingredients.cutPrep: sandwich slices, crusts removed, torn small

instructions: Toss the banana slices with the sugar and chill at least 30 minutes.
Dissolve the condensed milk and salt in the coconut milk.
Tear the bread small, soak it in the coconut milk mixture and leave 15 minutes.
Gently fold in two thirds of the bananas. Pour into a buttered baking tin, level the top and lay the remaining banana slices over it.

Bake at 350°F (175°C) with bottom heat only for 15 minutes, brush with the melted butter, then bake with top and bottom heat about 30 minutes more, until the bananas caramelise and the edges are golden.
Cool completely, then chill a few hours or overnight until set. Serve cold; it keeps 7 to 10 days in the fridge.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the sugar on and in the cake.

recipes.curationNote: Helen's Recipes, Bánh Chuối Nướng for every amount and step; 6 to 8 slices, scaled from 7 to our 10 (x1.4): 500 g bananas, 2 to 3 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp rum (optional), 2 tbsp sweetened condensed milk, a pinch of salt, 1 cup coconut milk, 6 slices crustless sandwich bread, 2 tbsp melted butter; 175°C bottom heat 15 minutes, brushed with butter, then 30 minutes top and bottom; chilled before serving.

recipes.name: Cà Phê Sữa Đá (Iced Milk Coffee)
recipes.flavorProfile: Strong, dark coffee dripped slowly through a phin over sweet condensed milk, stirred and poured over ice, bitter, sweet and creamy.
recipes.healthBenefit: Coffee brings caffeine and a little potassium; the condensed milk makes it a sweet drink.

ingredients.prepNote: from 2 tbsp dark-roast ground coffee dripped through a phin

instructions: Put the condensed milk in a glass and set the phin filter on top with the ground coffee.
Pour in a splash of hot water, wait 30 seconds for the grounds to bloom, then fill the filter.
Let it drip 4 to 5 minutes.
Stir the coffee into the condensed milk and pour over a glass of ice.

citations.source: Vicky Pham, Cà Phê Sữa Đá

recipes.curationNote: Vicky Pham, Cà Phê Sữa Đá for every amount and step; serves 1: 2 heaping tbsp ground coffee, 2 tbsp sweetened condensed milk, hot water, 1 cup ice.

recipes.name: Cà Phê Trứng (Egg Coffee)
recipes.flavorProfile: Hot strong coffee under a thick, sweet, custardy foam of egg yolk whipped with condensed milk, like a liquid tiramisu.
recipes.healthBenefit: The yolk brings choline and vitamin B12 and the coffee caffeine; with condensed milk it is a sweet treat.

ingredients.prepNote: use a very fresh or pasteurised egg
(from 8 g ground coffee and 110 g hot water, dripped through a phin)

instructions: Warm the phin and cup with a little hot water and pour it off.
Put the coffee in the phin, wet it with a splash of hot water for 30 seconds, then add the rest and let it drip 2 to 3 minutes.
Whisk the yolks with the condensed milk about 3 minutes, until pale, thick and frothy.
Spoon the egg cream over the hot coffee and serve straight away.
recipes.curationNote: Hungry Huy, Vietnamese Egg Coffee for every amount and step; serves 1: 8 g coffee brewed with 110 g water, 2 pasteurized egg yolks, 37 g condensed milk; no sugar or vanilla.

recipes.name: Sinh Tố Bơ (Avocado Shake)
recipes.flavorProfile: A thick, cold, pale green shake of ripe avocado blended with ice, milk and condensed milk, creamy and sweet.
recipes.healthBenefit: Avocado brings monounsaturated fat, fibre and potassium; the condensed milk adds sugar, so it is a sweet drink.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Put the avocado, condensed milk, milk and ice in a blender.
Blend 30 to 60 seconds until thick and smooth.
Taste and add a little more milk if you want it thinner.
Pour into glasses and serve right away.

citations.source: Viet World Kitchen, Avocado Shake (Sinh Tố Bơ)

recipes.curationNote: Viet World Kitchen, Avocado Shake (Sinh Tố Bơ) for every amount and step; serves 1, doubled for our 2: 1/2 avocado, 1/2 cup ice, 2 generous tbsp condensed milk, about 1/3 cup (90 ml) milk, optional pinch of salt.

recipes.name: Bánh Da Lợn (Steamed Layer Cake)
recipes.flavorProfile: Bouncy, chewy steamed layers of green pandan and golden mung bean, sweet with coconut milk, peeled apart one layer at a time.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly starch and sugar with a little protein from the mung beans; a sweet treat.

ingredients.cutPrep: split and peeled, soaked and steamed

ingredients.name: pandan leaves
ingredients.cutPrep: blended with a little of the water and strained

instructions: Warm the coconut milk, water, sugar and salt until the sugar dissolves, and cool to warm.
Whisk this into the tapioca starch and rice flour for a thin batter, then divide it in two.
Blend the steamed mung beans into one half, and the pandan juice into the other.
Oil a 20 cm tin and steam a thin layer of green batter 5 to 7 minutes until set, then a layer of yellow, alternating to the top.
Steam the last layer 10 to 15 minutes, cool completely, at least 4 hours, and slice with an oiled knife.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the tapioca starch and rice flour.
From the syrup in the batter.

recipes.curationNote: Helen's Recipes, Bánh Da Lợn for every amount and step; one 20 cm cake listed as 8 servings; ours cuts the same cake into 12 thinner slices.

recipes.name: Sữa Đậu Nành (Soy Milk)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fresh, warm soy milk scented with pandan and lightly sweetened, creamy and nutty, sold in bags from street carts in the morning.
recipes.healthBenefit: Soy milk brings plant protein and some potassium and folate; homemade, it carries no added calcium unless you add it.

ingredients.cutPrep: soaked 10 to 12 hours, shrivelled beans removed, rinsed well
450 ml for blending the pandan, 900 ml for cooking

instructions: Soak the soybeans overnight. Pick out any shrivelled beans and rinse several times so the milk does not taste beany.
Rinse the pandan leaves, blend them with 450 ml water, strain and let the liquid settle.
Put the soybeans, 900 ml water and the pandan water in a soy milk maker and run it, about 30 minutes; it switches off when done.
Strain the milk once more and stir in the sugar. Drink warm, or chill.

citations.source: Cookpad Vietnam (Bếp của Quỳnh), Sữa đậu nành lá dứa

recipes.curationNote: Cookpad Vietnam (Bếp của Quỳnh), Sữa đậu nành lá dứa for every amount and step; serves 4, scaled x1.5 to our 6: 100 g soybeans soaked overnight, 10 pandan leaves blended with about 300 ml water and strained, 600 ml water, sugar to taste and optional; cooked about 30 minutes in a soy milk maker, strained again.

recipes.name: Chè Trôi Nước (Sweet Rice Balls in Ginger Syrup)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, chewy glutinous rice balls filled with savory sweet mung bean paste, floating in a warm ginger brown-sugar syrup with sesame.
recipes.healthBenefit: The mung beans bring a little protein and fibre and the ginger warmth; mostly starch and sugar, so it is a festival treat.

components.note: a little in the filling, the southern way

ingredients.prepNote: (360 ml lukewarm for the dough, about 1 L for the syrup)

instructions: Cook the mung beans in 240 ml of the water until soft, mash with the sugar, salt, oil and fried shallots, and roll into 1 tbsp balls.
Work the lukewarm water into the glutinous rice flour a little at a time, knead, rest 30 minutes and knead again.
With oiled hands, flatten a piece of dough, wrap it around a filling ball with no gaps and roll smooth.
Boil the balls until they float, then 1 minute more.
Simmer the brown sugar and ginger in the rest of the water 5 to 10 minutes, add the balls and serve with sesame.
recipes.curationNote: Helen's Recipes, Chè Trôi Nước for every amount and step; serves 6 to 8 (22 balls): 200 g mung beans, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp sugar, 3 tbsp fried shallots, 3 tbsp oil; 400 g glutinous rice flour, 360 ml water; 300 g brown sugar, ginger, water; sesame to finish; no coconut cream. Taken at 6 servings.

recipes.name: Bánh Bò Nướng (Honeycomb Cake)
recipes.flavorProfile: A chewy, springy green pandan cake with a crisp golden crust and a honeycomb of tall bubbles inside, rich with coconut.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly starch, sugar and coconut fat with protein from the eggs; a sweet treat.

ingredients.name: pandan leaves
ingredients.cutPrep: blended with a little coconut milk and strained

ingredients.prepNote: in place of 1 bag of vanilla powder

instructions: Warm the coconut milk with the pandan juice and sugar until dissolved, and cool.
Whisk the eggs gently, without whipping in air, and stir into the coconut mixture.
Whisk in the tapioca starch, rice flour, baking powder, salt and vanilla, strain, and rest 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C) with the oiled bundt or cake pan inside for 10 minutes.
Pour the batter into the hot pan and bake 45 to 55 minutes until the top is deep golden, then cool upside down fully before slicing.
recipes.curationNote: Hungry Huy, Bánh Bò Nướng for every amount and step; one bundt cake, cut into our 12 slices; 2 bags of single-acting baking powder kept as 4 tsp.
